messages.author: a7170d46507a5631
messages.subject: Categorical contrast not working
parts:
Question about categorical analysis:
I get the same slope values when exchanging categorical variables.  I expect differences (since the data suggest that the UV will have the largest lambda, and trap catch count means were certainly not equal):

unique(d$trap) #BG (default intercept category), EVS, UV, CDC
d$trap.EVS <- ifelse( d$trap=="2" , 1 , 0 ) #"2" used to match cvs file
d$trap.UV <- ifelse( d$trap=="3", 1 , 0)
d$trap.CDC <- ifelse( d$trap=="4" , 1 , 0)
# Got a = 4.49 (mean) using BG as default intercept

#when I redo same calculation using EVS:
d$trap.BG <- ifelse( d$trap=="1" , 1 , 0 ) #EVS now default slope "a"
d$trap.UV <- ifelse( d$trap=="3", 1 , 0)
d$trap.CDC <- ifelse( d$trap=="4" , 1 , 0)
# Got a = 4.49 (mean) using EVS as default inercept

#model follows:
NAM1.0 <- map(
  alist(
    count ~ dpois( lambda ),
    log(lambda) <- a + bt.BG*trap.EVS + bt.UV*trap.UV + bt.CDC*trap.CDC,
    a ~ dnorm(0,10), 
    bt.BG ~ dnorm(0,1),
      bt.UV ~ dnorm(0,1),
      bt.CDC ~ dnorm(0,1)
  ),
  data = d)
precis(NAM1.0)

#Results for letting BG = intercept default
> precis(NAM1.0)
        Mean StdDev  5.5% 94.5%
a       4.49   0.04  4.43  4.55
bt.EVS -0.97   0.07 -1.08 -0.85
bt.UV   0.58   0.05  0.51  0.66
bt.CDC  0.10   0.05  0.01  0.18

#Results for letting EVS =  intercept default
> precis(NAM1.0)
        Mean StdDev  5.5% 94.5%
a       4.49   0.04  4.43  4.55
bt.BG  -0.97   0.07 -1.09 -0.86
bt.UV   0.58   0.05  0.50  0.65
bt.CDC  0.09   0.05  0.01  0.17

Please advise.

is here:

https://github.com/rmcelreath/rethinking

and the home page for the product is here:

http://xcelab.net/rm/statistical-rethinking/

but I didn't see a mailing list.

I don't mind people posting here about various packages that
use Stan or RStan, but the Stan developers are probably not
the best ones to answer most of these questions unless they
can be reduced to Stan itself as Daniel says.

- Bob
